text: The Fed has removed rate cut guidance and markets are now pricing rates rising to 4.2% by year-end, while CPI remains sticky at 3.4% and GDP growth is slowing to 1.5% — this combination of hotter inflation, potential rate hikes, and cooling growth creates a challenging backdrop for risk assets, so consider holding extra cash and being selective with new positions.

Trim QBTS to reduce your exposure — it's down 37%, has no earnings to support the valuation, and 22% short interest signals that a large number of professional traders are betting against it, so cut your risk and keep only a small speculative position if you still believe in the quantum computing story.
Raise your MSTR stop from $102.01 to $107.39 to lock in more downside protection on this volatile leveraged Bitcoin play, especially given the macro uncertainty around rising rates.

Micron looks compelling for adding shares — a price-to-earnings ratio of just 6.6 with nearly 49% revenue growth, a streak of beating expectations, and technical momentum turning positive make this one of the strongest value-plus-growth combinations in the portfolio right now.

Consider adding to Adobe — at a PE of just 9 with a nearly 10% free cash flow yield (meaning the company generates substantial cash relative to its stock price), this is unusually cheap for a dominant software franchise, even in a rising rate environment.

UnitedHealth's pullback of nearly 10% with all technical signals bearish creates an opportunity to add to a fundamentally strong healthcare giant at a better price, though size the addition modestly given the uncertain macro backdrop.
